paragraphs: Perry Weather sells a weather safety platform that pairs monitoring hardware at a customer site with automated alerting, so an entire staff works from the same reading of conditions. The buyers it names are schools, cities, golf clubs, and industrial firms.

Stations at the customer location measure heat stress, lightning, precipitation, wind, and air quality, refreshing every five minutes in the mobile app and dashboard. Each organization writes its own thresholds and decides who gets notified when one is crossed. Alerts can go to phones or to an outdoor siren system. Countdown timers mark the moment it is safe to resume play or work. All-clears go out automatically once the threat has passed.

Colin Perry founded the company in 2013. It reports more than 5,000 organizations nationwide as customers. It also counts over 200 million alerts sent, covering hazards from heat stress to lightning. Arthur Ventures led a $15M Series B. The stated markets run across athletics, golf, parks and recreation, energy, and airports.
